intro: A landmark heatmap may spread confidence over several pixels. Use every nonnegative value to estimate the expected row and column.
task: Return each heatmap’s total mass and mass-weighted center in zero-based row-column coordinates.
requirements: heatmaps has shape batch-by-height-by-width, contains nonnegative values, and every map has strictly positive total mass.
Return {"mass": vector, "centers": batch-by-2 matrix}. centers[b,0]=sum(row*mass)/total and centers[b,1]=sum(column*mass)/total. Heatmaps need not already sum to one.

Use finite real numeric values of magnitude at most 1e6, excluding boolean inputs. Each array axis has 1..64 entries and at most 65536 elements total unless a stricter bound is stated. Return NumPy arrays for array outputs, preserve caller inputs, and raise ValueError for invalid inputs.

examples.name: Uniform map
examples.output:
{'mass': [6.0], 'centers': [[0.5, 1.0]]}
(NumPy arrays shown as lists; rounded to 12 significant digits.)

examples.name: Single peak
examples.output:
{'mass': [2.0], 'centers': [[1.0, 1.0]]}
(NumPy arrays shown as lists; rounded to 12 significant digits.)

examples.name: Two weighted peaks
examples.output:
{'mass': [4.0], 'centers': [[0.0, 1.5]]}
(NumPy arrays shown as lists; rounded to 12 significant digits.)

hints.title: Follow the data
hints.body: Build row and column coordinate grids and weight each by the heatmap.

hints.title: Check the boundary
hints.body: Scale an entire heatmap by a positive factor; its center should stay unchanged.

explanation: Center of mass uses the whole spatial confidence distribution instead of only its maximum. It can produce subpixel coordinates between discrete pixel locations.

A multimodal map may place the center between two plausible peaks where little mass exists. The estimate describes the distribution’s mean, so applications should also consider its shape or uncertainty.
